ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two free drafters in one block, the target's own n-gram pool first and context lookup after
PROPOSAL: Lookahead decoding collects n-grams from the target's own parallel trajectories at zero extra forward passes; prompt lookup collects n-grams from the context. We fill the first positions of every draft block from the trajectory pool, which tracks what the target is about to say, and the later positions from the context, which is cheaper and longer, and we tune the hand-over position per category. Targets are Llama-3-8B-instruct and Qwen2-7B-instruct on Spec-Bench, and we record walltime speedup over plain decoding and accepted tokens per target pass.
CONTROLS: Context lookup on its own and the trajectory pool on its own, each at its best block length, which the mixed block has to lead to be worth building; the reversed order, context first and pool after, since the ordering is the claim; outputs checked token by token against greedy decoding; and timings repeated with warm caches.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The mixed block should lead both single drafters on chat and reasoning and tie context lookup on summarisation, and the reversed order should trail. If the reversed order does as well, position does not matter and the pool adds only acceptance, not ordering.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two free drafters in one block, the target's own n-gram pool first and context lookup after, set against trained drafters
PROPOSAL: Targets are Llama-3-8B-instruct and Qwen2-7B-instruct on Spec-Bench, and we record walltime speedup over plain decoding and accepted tokens per target pass. Lookahead decoding collects n-grams from the target's own parallel trajectories at zero extra forward passes; prompt lookup collects n-grams from the context. We fill the first positions of every draft block from the trajectory pool, which tracks what the target is about to say, and the later positions from the context, which is cheaper and longer, and we tune the hand-over position per category so that the free block can be placed among drafters that needed training.
CONTROLS: A trained EAGLE head and a trained Medusa head on the same targets, each at its best block length, which the mixed block is placed against to rank it among trained methods; plain decoding at the same block length, since the speedup is the claim; outputs checked token by token against greedy decoding; and timings repeated with warm caches.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The mixed block should land below both trained drafters on chat and reasoning and near them on summarisation, and plain decoding should trail. If the trained drafters do as well on summarisation, context repetition does not matter and training adds only acceptance, not ordering.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Handing over from early-exit drafting to context lookup when the exit's confidence drops
PROPOSAL: An early-exit copy of the target drafts token by token and reads its own top probability at each position; as soon as that probability falls under a threshold the block is completed by prompt lookup, so that the costly drafter is spent only where it is sure and the free drafter covers the rest. The threshold is tuned per category on held-out prompts, and the hand-over costs one comparison per position. Targets are Vicuna-7B and Llama-2-13B-chat over all six Spec-Bench categories, with the mixed stream of all categories as the deployment case, and we record walltime speedup over plain decoding and the share of accepted tokens drafted by each source.
CONTROLS: Early-exit drafting on its own and context lookup on its own at their best block lengths on every category, which the hand-over has to lead; a hand-over at a fixed position chosen per category, which separates confidence from position; the threshold tuned on one category and carried to the others; outputs checked against greedy decoding; and timings repeated.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: The confidence hand-over should lead the fixed-position hand-over most on chat and reasoning, where the exit's certainty varies along the response, and should tie it on summarisation. If the fixed position does as well everywhere, the exit's probability is not a usable signal and the gain is positional.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Handing over from early-exit drafting to context lookup when the exit's confidence drops, on repetitive inputs
PROPOSAL: Targets are Vicuna-7B and Llama-2-13B-chat over the summarisation and retrieval-augmented categories of Spec-Bench, with the most repetitive prompts as the deployment case, and we record walltime speedup over plain decoding and the share of accepted tokens drafted by each source. An early-exit copy of the target drafts token by token and reads its own top probability at each position; as soon as that probability falls under a threshold the block is completed by prompt lookup, so that the costly drafter is spent only where it is sure and the free drafter covers the rest. The threshold is tuned per context length on held-out prompts.
CONTROLS: Early-exit drafting on its own and context lookup on its own at their best block lengths on the two categories, which the hand-over has to lead; a hand-over at a fixed position chosen per context length, which separates confidence from position; the threshold tuned on short contexts and carried to long ones; outputs checked against greedy decoding; and timings repeated.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: The confidence hand-over should lead the fixed-position hand-over most on long contexts, where repeated spans are frequent, and should tie it on short ones. If the fixed position does as well everywhere, the exit's probability is not a usable signal and the gain is positional.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choosing the skipped layers of a self-draft by what the cascade gains
PROPOSAL: The layer-skipping drafter needs a set of layers to drop; we select that set by a short search that scores each candidate set by the walltime of the complete cascade, layer skipping above prompt lookup, on a held-out slice of each Spec-Bench category, with Mistral-7B-instruct and Llama-3-8B-instruct as targets. The search drops layers greedily from the full model and keeps a drop whenever the cascade's walltime improves, which couples the drafter's cost and its acceptance in one number instead of trading them by hand.
CONTROLS: The skipped set chosen by the heuristic of dropping layers whose output is most similar to their input, the usual training-free rule; the set chosen by acceptance rate on its own; each set run in the full cascade and timed on the remaining prompts of every category against lookup on its own; outputs checked against greedy decoding; and timings repeated.
COST: 88
PREDICTION: The walltime-chosen set should lead the similarity-chosen set on reasoning and chat and tie it on summarisation, where lookup carries the block. If the acceptance-chosen set does as well, cost barely varies across sets and acceptance is the whole story.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choosing the skipped layers of a self-draft by how close its predictions stay to the target
PROPOSAL: The search drops layers greedily from the full model and keeps a drop whenever the drafter's agreement with the target improves per dropped layer, which couples the drafter's depth and its fidelity in one number instead of trading them by hand. The layer-skipping drafter needs a set of layers to drop; we select that set by a short search that scores each candidate set by the top-one agreement between the skipped copy and the full target over a held-out slice of each Spec-Bench category, with Mistral-7B-instruct and Llama-3-8B-instruct as targets, and we report the chosen depth per category.
CONTROLS: The skipped set chosen by the heuristic of dropping layers whose output is most similar to their input, the usual training-free rule; the set chosen by the drafter's perplexity on its own; each set scored by agreement and perplexity on the remaining prompts of every category against the full target; outputs checked against greedy decoding; and timings repeated.
COST: 88
PREDICTION: The agreement-chosen set should lead the similarity-chosen set on reasoning and chat and tie it on summarisation, where the sets overlap most. If the perplexity-chosen set does as well, agreement barely varies across sets and perplexity is the whole story.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-free cascades under temperature sampling, against lookup under the same sampling
PROPOSAL: Speculative decoding stays lossless under sampling through rejection sampling on the draft and target distributions, but acceptance drops when the target's distribution is flat. We run a cascade of layer skipping above prompt lookup on Llama-2-7B-chat and Qwen2.5-7B-instruct at temperature one with a shared random state, over all Spec-Bench categories, and ask if the cascade still pays once both levels lose acceptance. We record walltime speedup over plain sampling and accepted tokens per target pass, and we log the block lengths and the random state of every run.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup on its own under the same temperature and random state, which the cascade must lead to be worth building; the layer-skipping drafter on its own under the same sampling; block lengths retuned at temperature one for every configuration, since the greedy lengths may be too long; samples checked for distributional identity with plain sampling by token frequency; and timings repeated.
COST: 20
PREDICTION: The cascade should keep a lead over lookup on chat and reasoning at temperature one, smaller than under greedy decoding, and lose it on summarisation. If the lead vanishes everywhere, the self-draft's acceptance under sampling is too low to pay for its passes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-free cascades under temperature sampling, against the same cascade under greedy decoding
PROPOSAL: We run a cascade of layer skipping above prompt lookup on Llama-2-7B-chat and Qwen2.5-7B-instruct at temperature one with a shared random state, over all Spec-Bench categories, and ask how much of the greedy speedup survives once both levels lose acceptance. Speculative decoding stays lossless under sampling through rejection sampling on the draft and target distributions, but acceptance drops when the target's distribution is flat. We record walltime speedup over plain sampling and accepted tokens per target pass.
CONTROLS: The same cascade under greedy decoding with the same random state, which sets what the cascade reaches when acceptance is highest; the same cascade at temperature one half; block lengths kept from the greedy configuration for every temperature, since the block length is the quantity held still; samples checked for distributional identity with plain sampling by token frequency; and timings repeated.
COST: 20
PREDICTION: The cascade should keep most of its greedy speedup at temperature one half and less at temperature one, with the largest drop on chat. If the drop is the same everywhere, the self-draft's acceptance under sampling falls uniformly with temperature.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Routing draft positions between self-draft and lookup by the kind of token expected
PROPOSAL: We log, for Llama-3-8B-instruct and Qwen2-7B-instruct on Spec-Bench, the acceptance of a layer-skipping self-draft and of prompt lookup per token type, grouping tokens into function words, numbers, code symbols, named entities and other content words, and we build a static rule that routes each draft position to the drafter with the higher logged acceptance per unit of latency for the type the previous token predicts. The rule is fitted on one half of the prompts per category and applied on the other half, and we record walltime speedup over plain decoding and the share of positions routed to each drafter.
CONTROLS: The best cascade with a single drafter assignment per level; lookup on its own and the self-draft on its own; a routing rule fitted on token types permuted across positions, which keeps the rule's shape while removing its information; outputs checked against greedy decoding; and timings repeated.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Routing should send numbers and code symbols to the self-draft and function words to lookup, and lead the single-assignment cascade most on arithmetic and translation. If the permuted rule does as well, the gain comes from mixing drafters and not from the token types.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Routing draft positions between self-draft and lookup by the kind of token expected, across precision and template choices
PROPOSAL: The rule is fitted once on one half of the prompts per category and then applied on the other half under each precision format and chat template, and we record walltime speedup over plain decoding and the share of positions routed to each drafter. We log, for Llama-3-8B-instruct and Qwen2-7B-instruct on Spec-Bench, the acceptance of a layer-skipping self-draft and of prompt lookup per token type, grouping tokens into function words, numbers, code symbols, named entities and other content words, and we build a static rule that routes each draft position to the drafter with the higher logged acceptance per unit of latency for the type the previous token predicts.
CONTROLS: The routed cascade run in half precision and in brain-float format; the routed cascade with the chat template and with plain concatenation of turns; a routing rule fitted on token types from the other model, which keeps the rule's shape while changing its source; outputs checked against greedy decoding; and timings repeated.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Routing should send numbers and code symbols to the self-draft and function words to lookup, and keep the same speedup under either precision and template, most clearly on arithmetic and translation. If the other model's rule does as well, the token types transfer across models and not only the mixing of drafters.
